items.stem: A child view must read and change a value owned by its parent. Which property wrapper should the child use for that value?

options.rationale: Correct: @Binding gives the child read-write access to state owned elsewhere without duplicating it.
@State declares new state owned by this view, not a reference to the parent's value.
A plain let is read-only and cannot write back to the parent.
@Environment reads shared context, not a specific parent-owned value passed down explicitly.

items.explanation: Correct: @Binding gives the child read-write access to state owned elsewhere without duplicating it.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about SwiftUI view modifiers are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Modifier order can change the final layout and appearance
options.rationale: Correct: each modifier wraps the previous result, so order matters.

options.text: A modifier returns a new view rather than mutating the original
options.rationale: Correct: modifiers are value-returning; SwiftUI views are value types.

options.text: Modifiers can only be applied once per view
options.rationale: The same modifier can be applied multiple times with different effects.

options.text: Modifiers execute imperatively at call time like UIKit setters
options.rationale: They describe a declarative view tree, not immediate imperative mutations.

items.explanation: Correct: each modifier wraps the previous result, so order matters.

items.stem: Where should a SwiftUI view start an asynchronous fetch tied to its lifecycle?

options.rationale: Correct: .task starts work when the view appears and cancels it when the view disappears.
body can run many times; side effects there cause repeated, uncontrolled work.
init runs during view construction and has no lifecycle or cancellation.

options.text: In a global function called at launch
options.rationale: That is not tied to the view and cannot be cancelled with it.

items.explanation: Correct: .task starts work when the view appears and cancels it when the view disappears.
